title: The Living Hope: Christ's Resurrection and Our Hope in Him
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro
summary: Drawing from 1 Peter 1:3-9, Pastor Lyro explains how Christ's resurrection provides the foundation for a living hope that sustains believers through trials. The sermon emphasizes that our hope is not in worldly circumstances but in Christ's death and resurrection, which guarantees our eternal inheritance and preservation until we see Jesus face to face.

outline.title: The Nature of Human Hope
subpoints: People cannot live without hope
What we hope in determines the quality of our life
We are created in God's image to be hopeful people

outline.title: False Hopes vs. True Hope
subpoints: Hope in becoming a better Christian to solve life problems is misplaced
Hope in God owing us something based on our performance is false
The only true hope is Jesus Christ, who died and yet lives
Things are simple: our hope is in Christ

outline.title: God the Father's Gracious Initiative
subpoints: God has caused us to be born again through His abundant mercy
Our hope originates with God, not with ourselves
God is gracious, merciful, kind, and awesome
God is not a detached being waiting to punish us
God sent His only Son to redeem us and bring us close to Him

outline.title: The Resurrection as the Basis of Our Hope
subpoints: Christ's resurrection is a historical, undebatable fact
Everything in our relationship with God is based on Christ's work
We cannot be saved without believing in Christ
Christ is the firstfruits of those to be raised from the dead

outline.title: The Living Hope and Our Inheritance
subpoints: We are born again into a living hope—alive like Jesus is alive
Our hope is a certainty, not mere wishful thinking
We have a future, imperishable, undefiled inheritance reserved in heaven
The ultimate inheritance is eternal life with Jesus Christ
Our joy in this life depends on setting our treasure on eternity

outline.title: God's Preservation Through Faith
subpoints: We are kept by the power of God through faith until salvation is fully revealed
Nothing can separate us from the love of God in Christ
We are guarded by Christ so we cannot escape His grace
God preserves us through faith until we see Jesus face to face
Believers support one another in their faith journey to eternity

outline.title: Trials and the Purification of Faith
subpoints: Our sufferings are brief moments compared to eternity
Trials strengthen and purify our faith
Various trials test our faith to praise, honor, and glory of Christ
Trials include saying no to sinful desires, being rejected, and living counter to worldly values
Our usefulness and joy now depend on having hope set on the resurrection

outline.title: The Practical Impact: Setting Our Hope on Christ
subpoints: We are to live with the joy of our unfading, imperishable hope
Whether circumstances improve or worsen, our hope remains unchanged
Our hope in resurrection gives energy and motivation to follow Jesus now
We should reject interim hopes tied to worldly success or comfort
Christ is our treasure, and serving Him flows from our hope in Him

transcript:
## Scripture Reading

> Now on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they and certain other women with them came to the tomb bringing the spices which they had prepared. But they found the stone rolled away from the tomb, then they went in and did not find the body of the Lord Jesus. And it happened as they were greatly perplexed about this that behold two men stood by them in shining garments. Then as they were afraid and bowed their faces to the earth, they said to them, Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen. Remember how he spoke to you when he was still in Galilee saying, The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men and be crucified and the third day rise again. And they remembered his words. Then they returned from the tomb and told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest. It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and the other women with them, who told these things to the apostles. And their words seemed to them like idle tales. And they did not believe them. But Peter arose and ran to the tomb and stooping down. He saw the linen cloths lying by themselves and he departed marveling to himself at what had happened. Then verse 34, The Lord is risen indeed and he has appeared to Simon. (Luke 24:1-13, 34)

## A Word to Those Without Faith

Let me start with a word to those of you who are with us today who do not believe in the Lord Jesus Christ. I'm very glad that you're here today, and I hope you hear every Sunday because this is where you need to be. We structure our service for those who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ to bring their praises and to honor their Savior. But there's power in that as you participate, as you see what we're doing, as you hear what we're saying, the Lord works in you.

I really hope that you listen to what I have to say today because what I have to say today is the difference between life and death for all of us. I want you to understand that all that I'm going to say is objectively true whether you believe it or not. Your belief in it is irrelevant for its truth. And though that's the case, it's only applied to you, only effective to you if you believe in the things that I'm going to say. So keep your ears open and listen to it. Join us as we consider the greatness of our Savior.

## People Cannot Live Without Hope

People cannot live without hope. But what we hope in will determine whether we have real life or a fake, joyless substitute. What you hope in determines the quality of your life. I've never met somebody who said, you know what, I just don't want to have any hope. I really just want to live a hopeless life. No one has ever said that. No matter whether you're a believer in Jesus Christ or not, you want hope in your life. And the reason for that is that we are created in the image of God to be hopeful people.

The apostle Peter has something to say to us today about hope because he knew hope and he knew what hope was because he met the risen Savior. Look at verses three through eight of 1 Peter, chapter one:

> Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his abundant mercy has begotten us again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead. (1 Peter 1:3-8)

The resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead is a historical, undebatable fact. What Peter is going to tell us today is what does that fact mean to us?

> It continues in verse four to an inheritance, incorruptible and undefiled and that does not fade away reserved in heaven for you, who are kept by the power of God through faith for salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. In this you greatly rejoice though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved by various trials that the genuineness of your faith be much more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tested by fire, may be found to praise, honor, and glory at the revelation of Jesus Christ, whom having not seen you love, though now you do not see him yet believing you rejoice with joy inexpressible and full of glory, receiving the end of your faith, the salvation of your souls. (1 Peter 1:4-9)

## False Hopes

Brothers and sisters, I would dare say that some of you are here today thinking that if only you could be a better Christian, you wouldn't be having the problems that you're having in your marriage with your children, with your parents, with your job, or whatever it is that you are having problems in life with. Or you're hoping that if you perform in a certain way, God is going to be more pleased with you and your hope is going to increase. But I'm here to tell you that if that is where your hope is, you're in trouble. Your hope is in the wrong place. And that's the bad news. There's lots of good news coming up, so hold on to that.

Some of you are here thinking that God owes you something, and you're here to get it. You're here to demand something from God. You've done these things, and God now owes you something. Well, more bad news. You too are hoping in a false hope.

Peter says here that there is one place and one place only for the Christian hope. And it is not in the things that are hard now, the hope is not that the things that are hard now will get easier later. It is not that things that are hard now will be resolved later. It's not that the problems that are weighing us down now will go away. The only hope we have in life or in death is Jesus Christ, who died and yet lives. That's the only hope.

Things are simple. We turn them into complicated things. A lot of times, if you're visiting with us, let me let you in a secret among Christians. When a Christian says, oh, this is complicated, that's code word. You know what it's code word for? I just don't want to do it or believe it. Because really, at the end of the day, things are simple. Our hope is in Christ, the one who died and yet lives.

## Our Hope Starts with God

Our hope starts with God, not with us. That's what Peter tells us in verse three:

> Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his abundant mercy has begotten us again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead. (1 Peter 1:3)

God, our Father and the Father of the Lord Jesus Christ has graciously done something for us. He has caused us to be born again. Peter cannot get away from the realization of the graciousness, the mercifulness, the loving kindness of God, the Father. Peter is overflowing with a sense of how kind and how loving and how gracious and how merciful God, the Father is.

So believer, I want to ask you a question. Is that how you think of God? When you run into those places in your marriage, or in your work, or with your children, or with your parents, or in your life in general when once again you seem to be just rounding the corner. Things seem to be getting better. And then your knees get taken out from under you and you fall on your behind. What is the first thought that comes to your mind? Is the first thought, Lord, you always do this to me. I'm that far from things getting better and you do this to me. Why do you do this to me?

I dare say that in moments of honesty, we would admit that that tends to be the way that we think about God. And if this is how we think of God, you don't know who God the Father is. He is more gracious than you could possibly comprehend. He is merciful, he is kind, and all of the good things that I'm about to tell you flow from him and from his grace and mercy and kindness. And Peter wants those who read this epistle to think of God, because God is great.

Who has seen the Lego movie? What's the theme of the Lego movie? Everything is awesome, right? Everything is not awesome. Is that fair to say? If you check your pulse and there is a pulse, everything is not awesome. But you know who is awesome? God is. And that's the Father of our Lord, Jesus Christ. And that's important for us to notice that Peter doesn't bring before us any God out there. The God he's speaking about is not the God of Alcoholics Anonymous, a power higher than yourself. The God that Peter says is gracious and kind and merciful and awesome is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. That is the only God.

How we think of God really matters. He's not a detached being that sits in heaven waiting for us to mess up so he can punish us. And I think we often think of God that way—that he's just around the corner trying to catch us doing something wrong so he can punish us. That's not the God of the Bible. The God of the Bible sent his own, only begotten son, his one and unique son to redeem us and to bring us close to him so that we can be with him for all eternity. And because of that, because of all that, our God who is the Father of the Lord Jesus Christ is worthy of praise.

## Praising God

Peter says: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. In verse three, the word blessed literally means one who is spoken well of. We could use the word praise here. Praise be the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

In the Bible, to praise God is not simply to sing songs with our eyes closed, our hands swaying in the air. To praise God is to brag about him, to boast about him, to be proud of him, to be satisfied with him. And if you have kids you know what I'm talking about. Have you ever been at the game where your kid does something good and then he's like, that's my son, that's my daughter right there. Did you see what they just did? Or these days now, picture after picture of the grandkids, till somebody's sick and tired of it, though I know there's no way you could be sick and tired of my grandkids because they're so cute. We know what it means to brag about somebody. That's what our God is worthy of. To be made much of in our lives.

And why? Why is he worthy of praise? Brothers and sisters, because he's saving us. Peter is putting things in perspective by reminding us that though we may have a trying life, God is saving us.

## The Foundational Doctrine of Salvation

All the foundational doctrines of a Reformed understanding of the Bible are here in this passage that we read today. God has caused us to be born again. He has effectively called us out of darkness and translated us into the kingdom of the sun. He has given us a new birth. We have not been able to resist his grace. You see that in verse three, and that's what the word translated "begotten" means—it has caused us to be born again. God reached down to us through the proclamation of his word. He changed our hearts and gave us a new life.

One of my favorite Psalms is Psalm 40. And if you're counting, if you're keeping track of my favorite Psalms, there's about 149 of them. But in Psalm 40, the Psalmist gives us words to our experience, where he is in the bottom of the pit, the miry pit. So picture a well that has no water but is full of mud. And it's the kind of mud that the more you move, the more you sink. And that's where the psalmist is. That's where he finds himself in the beginning of the psalm. And he looks up, there's darkness. He looks down, there's darkness. And then he says that the Lord took him out of the miry pit, set his feet upon the rock. Guess what you can't do on the rock? Sink. He exalted him, he lifted him up. And then he gave him a new song. What is that new song? Whatever song it is that praises Jesus. Holy is the lamb. Holy, holy, holy. Lord God Almighty.

Why did he do that? Because you're such a great person? Because he just could not be without you? Because he needed your skillset to accomplish his plan? No. In verse two of 1 Peter, Peter says that he did that because of his predestining foreknowledge. And here Peter tells us that God calls us to be born again because of his great mercy. Not because we deserved to be born again, but because he's merciful. His choosing of us is not based or conditioned on anything that we have done. It's conditioned on his desire and his desire only.

## How God is Saving Us

How is God the Father saving us? By the way, if you look at verse five and then verse nine, Peter uses the word salvation here to describe the entire journey of the elect from the moment of being born again to the moment where you see Jesus face to face at the resurrection. How is God the Father saving us? Verse three says through the work of the Lord Jesus Christ, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.

As most of you know, we meet on Sundays to celebrate the resurrection of Christ. Every Sunday is Easter. So for those of you in this church, except for Easter, every Sunday is Easter. So if that's your motivation, see you next Sunday. We meet on the first day of the week, not the first day of the month, because Christ rose from the dead. And through that work of Christ, God is saving us.

He only mentions the resurrection here, but he cannot be raised from the dead if he wasn't first dead. Does it make sense? So the resurrection includes the death. And he could not die, simple logic, he could not die if he wasn't alive first. So the resurrection also includes his life. Everything in our relationship with God is based on Christ's work as the God-man.

And you might think, I can't do anything about it? No, you can't, other than believe. And brothers and sisters, that's glorious, because the same way that you cannot do anything for God to choose you, there's nothing you can do for him to let you go. You get that? You don't have that power. You are in the hands of God, in the hands of Christ, and you're not going to be let go.

## The Elect and the Inheritance

And he'd done all this for you. See that in verse four? And the question is, who is the "you"? Well, verses one and two tell us that the "you" are the elect pilgrims. Christ lived, died, and came back to life for the elect. His atonement, his death is particular to a group of people. You know how big that group of people are? It's more numerous than all the stars of heaven. It's more numerous than the grains of sand on the seashore.

So if you want to know eventually how many people are going to be in heaven, here's a job for Henry. You can invite another Henry to go with you. So the two Henrys, you're going to go to a park on the sound that has sand on the shore. Then you're going to count every grain of sand in that one park. And then you go to the Pacific and you count every grain of sand. And then you go to the Atlantic shore, and by the time you're done with the United States, there's other shores. That's how many people God will eventually have in heaven.

How do you know that you're part of the elect? Simply. Remember, this is not complicated, people. I believe in Jesus Christ. The question is not, am I elect? The question is, do I believe in Jesus Christ? That's it. And that settles the matter. And those who are born again come to faith in Christ and are preserved by God through that faith to the end.

In verse five it says we are preserved all the way to the coming of Jesus Christ. The saints are persevered all the way to the end. God will preserve every last one of us. We have genuine faith all the way till we see Jesus face to face. And how are we preserved in Christ?

Jack, come over here. So how are we preserved in Christ? Jack drags me to eternity, drag me to eternity. And I drag Jack. And together we bring each other all the way to eternity. Do you get that? Jerry drags Linda, Lena drags Adam, Adam drags Kim, Kim drags Renee, who drags Paul, who drags Leo, who drags him. We together, thank you, we together arrive at the end. And you visitor who don't go to church often, you don't have that. And because of that, if you remain that way, you will not arrive at the end. You're going to arrive somewhere else, but not in the presence of Christ.

## We Are Kept by the Power of God

This word that he has translated as "kept" is important. He says:

> Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his abundant mercy has begotten us again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, to an inheritance incorruptible and undefiled... who are kept by the power of God through faith for salvation. (1 Peter 1:3-5)

This word "kept" means to be guarded, not only so that attacks from the outside cannot separate us from God, but also so that we can't escape either. Because if we're left to ourselves, we would escape God. And yet if Christ has died for you, God is not going to let you escape.

And Paul expands on that in Romans chapter eight, when he asks:

> What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us? If Jesus Christ, brothers and sisters, is in heaven, pleading for you, who on this creation can come before God and bring an accusation against you? Satan? No. Who can separate you from the love of God in Jesus Christ? (Romans 8:31-32, 33-34, 35)

Christ is risen. So no one. Not life, not death, not angels in heaven, not other people, not even yourself. Because Christ is risen. And because Christ is risen, you're being kept for all eternity.

## Born Again Into a Living Hope and an Inheritance

And Paul tells us that God causes us to be born again into two things. In verse three, we're born again into a hope that is alive, a living hope. Some traditions say a lively hope, but it's a hope that is alive. A hope that's alive just like Jesus is alive. Our hope is also alive.

And hope here is not a wishful thing. You know how I say, oh, are you going to go to somebody's house today after church? Oh, I hope so. That's not the case. This is a certainty that something good is going to happen. This is a hope that gives life. That is, it motivates the Christian. It gets him and gets her going in his or her following of Jesus Christ.

And what is the good thing that Christians are looking for that they're certain will happen? The resurrection when Christ returns. That's our hope. We live now for God's glory. We live now with joy. We live now in the service of Christ because we're going to be risen from the dead. And why? How do we know that? Because Christ is risen. And he's the first fruits of all those that are going to be risen from the dead.

Not only have we been born again to a lively hope, we also have been born again into an inheritance. In verse four, it is a future inheritance, but we don't have to worry about it because it will last till we get it. It is incorruptible. It is undefiled. And that inheritance, we see in verse nine, is not what you might think. You know how we read the book of Revelation, we get excited about the streets of gold and the gates of pearl and all that. But really the ultimate inheritance that we have is eternal life with Jesus Christ. That's what we're looking forward to.

And there's great joy in this life if we're looking forward to the life to come. Remember what Jesus, the Lord says in Matthew 6:21:

> Where your treasure is, so will your heart be. (Matthew 6:21)

If our treasure is in the life to come with Jesus at the resurrection, then our heart will be there. And this life, no matter what happens, will be full of joy, because we know that's the case.

So because Christ is risen, we have hope. And because Christ is risen now, the life we live now is a brief moment in light of eternity. Some of you were sick this week. Some of you are here pumped with Tylenol and cough suppressant in order to be here. And if you're a lady and you're sick, you just went about your business. If you're a guy and you're sick, you're laid in bed, and it's been the end of the world, and it looks like this is never going to end and it's forever. Some of you are very sick, closing to death. Some of you have all kinds of sufferings in your life. Some of you have been rejected by your family. Some of you have stories that if the angels in heaven would know them, they would weep. And yet Peter tells us that all of that is a brief moment in life compared to eternity to come.

## Our Trials and the Genuineness of Faith

So he says that in verses six and seven:

> In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved by various trials, that the genuineness of your faith being much more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tested by fire may be found to praise, honor, and glory at the revelation of Jesus Christ. (1 Peter 1:6-7)

You are grieved, you are distressed, you are tried, and that might even characterize most of your life. But whatever it is, it only lasts for a while in light of eternity. I'm not making light of your struggles, but we need to put this in perspective. Eternity is a long time and it's going to be glorious. And these various trials are the trials that come from being a Christian—having to say no to things that you naturally like to do. Our nature is not good. We don't want to do the things that we naturally want to do.

Being shunned and made fun of because you are not willing to go along with what everyone around you is doing. Living in a world that is opposed to what you think is important. Being punished for following the Lord. Broken family relationships because of your faith in Christ. Fighting illicit desires of the heart because the Lord tells you that it is best for you.

And as you go through these trials and it's heavy, your faith is purified, your faith is strengthened to the praise and the honor of the Lord Jesus Christ.

## What Christ's Resurrection Means for Our Lives

So how should this impact your life? Christ is risen, so what? You leave here today, go to your home. Hopefully you all have a place to go. If you don't come see me, come see Jim Hunter, come see Tim Vanderhoof. I'll look at the guest list first and make sure I... And we'll make sure you have a place to go.

And then what? What does a truth—a truth that Christ is risen, a truth that no matter how intelligent you are, there's no argument against. How's that going to shape you?

In Christ you have a life-changing, life-giving hope. If you have faith in Jesus Christ, if your trust is in Jesus Christ, you have a hope that nobody can touch and no one can take away because it is unfading and it is imperishable and it is undefiled and it's kept in heaven for you and God is guarding it for you and no one can mess with that hope. No circumstance in life can increase or diminish it.

Your joy and your usefulness in this life is tied to your receiving, your apprehension of that hope. If your hope is not set on the resurrection, then your joy will be diminished now and your usefulness also will be diminished now.

So let me ask you this: What are you hoping in now? Where is your hope right now? For some of you things have been hard and in God's kindness they're going to get better. For some of you things have been hard and they're going to get worse. But no matter where we are in those two categories, that is not where our hope is.

Our hope is in Jesus Christ. Our hope is in his death, in his resurrection and in our resurrection. Your hope is in Christ and that bears fruit now. The hope of your future resurrection is life-giving now as you follow Jesus.

Is this enough for you? Is this enough for you? Are you looking for an interim hope, a hope that goes between now and then, always looking for something now in your own time, in your own condition, in your own circumstances that you can cling to that is going to be the thing that gets you through? Have you had your hope in the wrong place?

If your hope is in the resurrection, it will give you the joy and the energy to live now, no matter what the successes and defeats are, no matter what the blessings and the trials are, because you know that in the end, neither the good things nor the bad things have the final word because your hope is waiting for you.

Where is your hope? Christ is risen.
